circuit.name: Semaphore
circuit.linkToArtifacts: Partly established. Each verification key equals the one inside the proving key Semaphore publishes for that tree depth (checked 2026-10-11). That those proving keys were built from this source in an honest trusted setup was not checked here.

publicFields.name: group root
publicFields.meaning: Merkle root of the list of membership commitments the proof refers to.

publicFields.name: nullifier
publicFields.meaning: A value derived from the prover's secret and the scope. The same secret and scope always give the same nullifier.

publicFields.name: hashed message
publicFields.meaning: Hash of the message this proof is bound to.

publicFields.name: hashed scope
publicFields.meaning: Hash of the scope, the topic within which the nullifier is fixed.

explanation.claim: Someone knew the secret behind a membership commitment included under this group root, and generated this proof bound to this message and scope.
hidden: Which membership commitment under the root was used.

applicationChecks.description: Whether any application currently accepts this group root. The root may be old or made up.
Whether this nullifier has been used before.

limits: This does not establish unique personhood: one person can hold several memberships.
This does not establish that membership was granted fairly.
This does not establish that whoever presents this file controls the credential: a proof can be copied.
Hiding which member made the proof is not anonymity. The message may identify someone, a small group hides little, and a repeated nullifier links proofs from the same member in the same scope.
assumptions: The Groth16 proof system and the BN254 curve are sound.
The trusted setup behind the verification keys was performed honestly.
The verification keys belong to the named circuit, and that circuit enforces the claim above.

review.note: Draft wording taken from the project owner's illustrative report. No qualified person has reviewed it against the circuit.
